task.title: Use a form for a real record
task.shortdesc: Choose the form that matches a record you have, such as the 1841 census, and see what it fills in for you.

prereq.p: Open the page of Patrick Brontë first. shows how.

context.p: Some records have a form of their own, with the boxes that the record has. The form for a census already knows the date of the census. This page opens the form for the 1841 census.

step.cmd: Choose in the part that starts , then choose .

info.p: The list scrolls. Turn the mouse wheel with the pointer on it to find the part. The list also has a button named , with a count in brackets, that shows the other forms, such as the later censuses.

step.cmd: Read the line at the top of the form.

stepresult.p: It says Adding to the household of and the name of the person, with a link named .
The date is already 6 June 1841, the night of the census. A line under it reads Reads as 6 June 1841.

result.p: You have chosen the form that matches the record. The form shows Census as its event type, the date in , and a box that must be filled in.
result.note: Good practice: copy what the record says, even if you think it is wrong. Put what you think in a note.
